title: User offers to share their password
symptom: User tries to give their password to the technician
user_description: My email isn't working. Here, let me write my password down so you can log in and sort it out for me.

options.text: Accept it but promise to forget it afterwards
options.why: Once you know the password the security promise is already broken. Passwords should only be known by their owner.

options.text: Ask him to email the password so you have it in writing
options.why: Makes it worse. Passwords in email can be read by others and stored forever.

options.text: Politely refuse, explain support never needs a password, and fix it with your own admin tools or a supervised remote session
options.why: Support has other ways to help without knowing a password. Refusing protects the user and teaches a safe habit.

hints: Should anyone besides the user know the password?
How could you still help without it?
real_world_tip: Say it kindly: 'I never need your password, and it's safer if nobody but you knows it.' Most users appreciate it.
